1.explanation: The root of the highlighting failure lies in the C-family grammar definitions for "class-name" in the clike and cpp language components. In components/prism-clike.js the pattern for "class-name" only matches simple class/trait/interface/new usages but does not catch names in an inheritance clause or scoped qualifiers. Similarly, in components/prism-cpp.js the "class-name" rule only recognizes standalone definitions (class/enum/struct) and ignores class names in member qualifiers and base specifiers. Fixing those two definitions (updating their regex to include colon-qualified and scope-qualified class names) will restore correct highlighting in both scenarios.
1.bug_scenario: When PrismJS highlights C++ code, it fails to recognize and style class names in two contexts: (1) after the colon in an inheritance list (e.g. QMainWindow in "class MainWindow : public QMainWindow" is not highlighted as a class name), and (2) in a method definition qualifier (e.g. MainWindow in "void MainWindow::changeWindowTitle()" is not highlighted).

2.explanation: Prism’s C-like grammar (in prism-clike.js) defines a “class-name” token that only matches keywords like class, interface, extends, etc., followed by an identifier, but it doesn’t cover C++-style inheritance (“: public Base”) so QMainWindow is never tokenized as a class name. The C++ grammar (in prism-cpp.js) similarly only matches class, enum, and struct declarations, not the inherited base classes or the qualifier in method definitions. Additionally, the generic ‘function’ rule in prism-clike.js (which underlies C++) only picks up bare identifiers before “(”, so it doesn’t catch the qualifier MainWindow in MainWindow::changeWindowTitle. These grammar rules must be extended to recognize C++ inheritance lists and qualified names.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting C++ code, PrismJS correctly highlights the class name in a definition (e.g. MainWindow), but it fails to highlight the base class in an inheritance declaration (QMainWindow in “class MainWindow : public QMainWindow”) and it also fails to highlight the class qualifier in a method definition (the “MainWindow” in “void MainWindow::changeWindowTitle()”).
